expectations.text: Output mentions Manski reflection problem or the linear-in-means identification failure
expectations.evidence: Explicit section titled 'The Manski Reflection Problem' with citation: 'This simultaneity creates a fundamental identification failure. The linear-in-means model... is algebraically problematic because the regressor (mean peer smoking) mechanically reflects back the individual's own outcome.' Also cited Manski (1993) by name.

expectations.text: Output mentions Shalizi-Thomas confounding or the homophily-contagion confound
expectations.evidence: Explicit section titled 'The Homophily-Contagion Confound': 'This is sometimes formalized in the Shalizi & Thomas (2011) result showing that homophily and contagion are generically unidentifiable from purely observational network data without strong assumptions.'

expectations.text: Output does NOT claim the regression identifies causal peer effects
expectations.evidence: Explicitly stated: 'cross-sectional regression cannot cleanly identify peer influence (social contagion)'; 'The 0.43 coefficient is a real and interesting finding — it tells you that, descriptively, students whose friends smoke more are more likely to smoke themselves... But it does not answer [the causal question].'; 'Your result is suggestive but not causal.'

expectations.text: Output correctly specifies that SAOM/RSiena requires longitudinal panel data with at least 2 waves AND observable network change between waves — NOT just cross-sectional data
expectations.evidence: Stated: 'SAOMs require longitudinal panel data with at least two waves — ideally three or more — where you observe both the network structure and the behavior at multiple time points, and where there is observable change in both the network and behavior between waves. You cannot apply RSiena to your current cross-sectional dataset.'

expectations.text: Output mentions Bramoullé et al. IV/GMM or friends-of-friends instruments as a cross-sectional identification strategy (not just 'use SAOM')
expectations.evidence: Dedicated section 'Option A: Instrumental Variables (Cross-Sectional Identification)': 'the key insight from Bramoullé, Djebbari & Fortin (2009) is that in a network with intransitive triads (friends-of-friends who are not your own friends), the characteristics of your friends' friends can serve as instruments for your friends' behavior.' This was presented as a distinct cross-sectional option before SAOM.
